chunks: What Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn 'Uthman, from Ibn Muskan, from Aban ibn Taghlib:
He said: I asked Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) about the one who is killed in the path of Allah — is he to be washed, shrouded, embalmed with hanut, and prayed over?
He said: He is buried just as he is, in his clothes — unless he had a breath of life remaining and then died, in which case he is washed, shrouded, and embalmed with hanut.
Verily the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed over Hamza and shrouded him, because he had been stripped [of his garments].

key_terms.جُرِّدَ: was stripped (of his garments); passive of jarrада — to denude, to remove clothing forcibly
key_terms.رَمَقٌ: last breath of life; the faintest lingering sign of life
key_terms.سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: the path of Allah; specifically denotes death in jihad (martyrdom)
key_terms.يُحَنَّطُ: to be embalmed with hanut — camphor and aromatic substances applied to the deceased's body before shrouding

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia fiqh on performing ghusl, kafan, and hanut for a martyr killed in battle?
ai.summary: Aban ibn Taghlib reports asking Imam al-Sadiq (AS) whether a martyr killed in battle requires ghusl, kafan (shrouding), hanut (embalming), and the funeral prayer. The Imam ruled that such a person is buried in his clothes as he is, unless he was found still alive and subsequently died — in which case full funeral rites apply. This ruling is grounded in the Prophet's (SAWW) own precedent at Uhud: he prayed over Hamza and shrouded him only because Hamza's garments had been stripped from his body.
